English.Char_Desc_450: Mira is a free AI voice assistant for Windows. Say the wake word ("Hey Mira") and talk to AI, get a 7-day weather forecast, launch apps and websites, set alarms and timers, and manage your schedule by voice. Speech recognition runs on your PC with Whisper. English.Char_Desc_2000:
Mira is a free AI voice assistant for Windows 10 and 11.
Wake word: Say "Hey Mira" (or a phrase you choose) and start talking. No button, no keyboard.
Talk to AI: Ask questions and get spoken answers. Mira works with cloud AI providers (Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible API) using your own API key, or with local LLMs through Ollama, LM Studio and Lemonade.
Everyday voice commands: 7-day weather forecasts, launching apps and websites with your own keywords (Voice Launcher), summarizing websites you register (Web Watch), alarms, timers, schedules, volume control and clipboard reading.
Screen Vision: Say "Look at the screen" and a cloud AI vision model (Gemini, Claude or OpenAI) explains what it sees.
Live mode (optional, off by default): Real-time voice conversation with Gemini Live.
Natural voices: Mira speaks with Edge TTS (needs Python with the edge-tts package), AivisSpeech or VOICEVOX (separate free apps that must be installed and running; they offer many character voices). Otherwise it uses the built-in Windows voice.
Memory: Mira can remember things you tell it, and you can review or delete them in the settings.
Your data: Wake word detection and speech recognition (Whisper) run on your PC, except in Live mode, which sends your microphone audio to Google's Gemini Live. With a cloud AI, your transcribed words and recent conversation go to that provider; with a local LLM and a local voice engine, conversations stay on your PC (if the local AI is not running at startup, Mira uses a cloud AI whose key is saved or set as an environment variable). Weather, search requests and Screen Vision use online services. Mira has no telemetry, and API keys are stored encrypted with Windows DPAPI.
What Mira does not do: It does not click or move the mouse for you. For full hands-free control of Windows, use Windows Voice Access alongside Mira.
Mira is completely free: no subscription, no trial, no license key.
